# Architecture catalog

Catalog date: 2026-11-16. For changing B2 product details, use <https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage> as the authority.

## Offload flight captures into a per-mission archive and trigger processing

After each flight, a field laptop, ground station or relay uploads stills, video, telemetry, flight logs and RTK/PPK files into a write-once per-mission prefix, writes manifest.json last, and a prefix-scoped B2 Event Notification starts downstream processing.

**Use when:** Drone teams collect data on SD cards spread across field crews and docks. They need a resumable, verifiable offload into one durable place, with chain of custody and a reliable processing trigger, without running a file server.

**Workflow:** rclone copy (native B2 backend, checksum verified) moves SD-card or staging folders into `raw/<client>/<site>/<mission-id>/`; a browser field portal can upload stills with presigned PUT URLs → Multi-GB video uses multipart upload, because a single PUT is capped at 5 GB → The uploader writes manifest.json last with mission, site, aircraft, camera, CRS and a file list with client-computed hashes → A B2 Event Notification rule on the raw/ prefix posts to an event broker, which ignores everything except */manifest.json before enqueuing jobs → A lifecycle rule cancels unfinished large-file uploads; raw captures are never moved or tiered → Object Lock retention or a legal hold protects raw captures kept as evidence → Vendor-cloud fleets (DJI Dock, FlightHub) land in the vendor cloud first; an rclone relay copies them to B2

**B2 capabilities:** S3-compatible API with a regional endpoint, Presigned PUT URLs for field and browser uploads (5 GB single-PUT limit), Multipart upload for multi-GB video, Event Notifications (prefix-filtered, optional signing secret, enabled through Backblaze Support), Object Lock (governance or compliance) and legal hold, Lifecycle rule to cancel unfinished large-file uploads, Application keys scoped to one bucket and name prefix with write and list capabilities per field crew; no object reads or permanent version deletion.

**Integrations:** [rclone](https://rclone.org/b2/) — Configure the native `b2` backend with an application key ID and key scoped to the crew's prefix (write and list); `rclone copy` resumes, skips files already in B2 and verifies SHA-1 on upload. The S3 backend with provider Other and endpoint `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com` also works ([setup guide](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-integrate-rclone-with-backblaze-b2)); [AWS SDK for Python (boto3)](https://boto3.amazonaws.com/v1/documentation/api/latest/reference/core/session.html) — Set endpoint_url to `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com` derived from B2_REGION, and set request_checksum_calculation and response_checksum_validation to `when_required` in botocore Config; worker code uses boto3 to read frames and write inference results for Ultralytics and Roboflow ([setup guide](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-use-the-aws-sdk-for-python-with-backblaze-b2)).

**Scale:** Bursty uploads after each flight, sized from image count, video bitrate and duration, and telemetry frequency. Standard B2 is the default; offload speed is usually bounded by the field uplink. Use rclone or SDK multipart concurrency for large video.

**Security:** Field crews hold write-plus-list keys scoped to `raw/<client>/`, without object reads or permanent version deletion; writeFiles still permits hiding or creating a new version of an existing key; For strict append-only field access, use a trusted upload relay that allocates new authorized keys and refuses replacements; presigned PUTs can be replayed until expiry, and Object Lock protects versions without preventing hiding or a new current version; Verify signed event POSTs when a signing secret is configured, and keep the receiver idempotent; Keep bucket, lifecycle and Object Lock administration keys out of field devices; This design uses scoped application keys for relay uploads; vendor-cloud exports are staged in the relay tier.

## Reconstruct orthomosaics, elevation models, point clouds and meshes from mission imagery

Stateless CPU/GPU workers pull a mission's raw images from B2, run SfM/MVS with OpenDroneMap NodeODM or COLMAP on local NVMe scratch, and write orthomosaic, DSM/DTM, LAZ point cloud, textured mesh and quality report to an immutable per-run prefix.

**Use when:** Teams reprocess missions when parameters or software change. They need inputs and every run's outputs kept side by side without a shared filesystem tying compute to storage.

**Workflow:** An event or an operator triggers a job for `raw/<client>/<site>/<mission-id>/` → The worker downloads images to local NVMe scratch and submits them to NodeODM (pyodm) or runs pycolmap → NodeODM uploads task-ID results to a dedicated client staging bucket with no key-prefix restriction; the publisher reads staging and writes the versioned products/ layout → Or the worker writes outputs with boto3 managed multipart to `products/<mission-id>/<run-id>/` → A run manifest.json records software versions, parameters, the input manifest hash and output keys; new run ids keep earlier runs immutable → Desktop tools without S3 support (Agisoft Metashape, PIX4Dmatic) are staged with rclone into the same layout → The run manifest landing triggers COG conversion, point cloud tiling and AI inspection

**B2 capabilities:** S3-compatible API with a regional endpoint, Multipart upload for multi-GB GeoTIFF, LAZ and mesh outputs, Per-run immutable prefixes with manifests (B2-side pattern), Lifecycle rules to expire superseded runs or staging prefixes, Event Notifications to chain downstream jobs, Scoped application keys (read raw/, write products/).

**Integrations:** [OpenDroneMap NodeODM](https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/NodeODM) — Start NodeODM with --s3_endpoint `s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`, a dedicated client staging bucket, --s3_upload_everything and --s3_acl none; supply credentials through AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY. The staging key has no name prefix because startup writes root test.txt and results use task-ID paths ([setup guide](https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/NodeODM/blob/master/config.js)); [AWS SDK for Python (boto3)](https://boto3.amazonaws.com/v1/documentation/api/latest/reference/core/session.html) — Set endpoint_url to `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com` derived from B2_REGION, and set request_checksum_calculation and response_checksum_validation to `when_required` in botocore Config; worker code uses boto3 to read frames and write inference results for Ultralytics and Roboflow ([setup guide](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-use-the-aws-sdk-for-python-with-backblaze-b2)); [rclone](https://rclone.org/b2/) — Configure the native `b2` backend with an application key ID and key scoped to the crew's prefix (write and list); `rclone copy` resumes, skips files already in B2 and verifies SHA-1 on upload. The S3 backend with provider Other and endpoint `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com` also works ([setup guide](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-integrate-rclone-with-backblaze-b2)).

**Scale:** Storage and scratch requirements depend on the image set, output formats, and reconstruction settings. Standard B2 is the default; workers are compute-bound. Keep SfM scratch on local NVMe and upload only finished products.

**Security:** Never leave NodeODM's default public-read ACL in place; pass --s3_acl none; Processing reads only raw/<client>/; NodeODM writes its dedicated staging bucket, and a separate publisher reads staging and writes products/ without deleting raw captures; Run manifests record input hashes so each product traces to its source captures.

## Serve orthomosaics and elevation models as cloud-optimized map layers

Orthomosaics, DEMs and index maps such as NDVI are converted to Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs in `cog/<mission-id>/` and read in place by TiTiler, QGIS, ArcGIS Pro, GeoServer and rasterio through HTTP range requests, with CDN or presigned client delivery and no stored tile pyramid.

**Use when:** Clients and analysts need to view and analyze multi-GB orthomosaics and DEMs without downloading them, and providers do not want to pre-render and store a second XYZ tile copy of every mission.

**Workflow:** A conversion job reads `products/<mission-id>/<run-id>/orthophoto.tif` and writes a COG with internal overviews to `cog/<mission-id>/<product>.tif` through GDAL /vsis3/ (rio-cogeo or gdal_translate -of COG) → TiTiler renders XYZ/WMTS tiles on demand from range GETs and accepts only validated layer ids, never raw URLs → QGIS, ArcGIS Pro and GeoServer open the same objects in place → Optional analytics jobs read only needed windows and write masks and GeoJSON to `analysis/<mission-id>/` → Public basemaps go through Cloudflare with B2 as origin; private deliverables go out as presigned GETs or through a signing Worker

**B2 capabilities:** S3-compatible API with HTTP range GETs, Presigned GET URLs for time-limited client delivery, CORS rules for browser map clients, CDN origin (Cloudflare partnership; see pricing for egress terms through partner CDNs), Scoped read-only application keys per consumer, Included egress (see B2 pricing for current terms).

**Integrations:** [GDAL /vsis3/](https://gdal.org/en/stable/user/virtual_file_systems.html) — Set `AWS_S3_ENDPOINT=s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com` (host only), AWS_REGION, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY; set AWS_VIRTUAL_HOSTING=FALSE for bucket names that contain dots ([setup guide](https://gdal.org/en/stable/user/virtual_file_systems.html#vsis3-aws-s3-files)); [Rasterio / rio-cogeo](https://github.com/rasterio/rasterio) — Pass rasterio.session.AWSSession(endpoint_url="s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com") to rasterio.Env, or set GDAL's AWS_S3_ENDPOINT; rio cogeo create writes COGs straight to /vsis3/ paths ([setup guide](https://github.com/rasterio/rasterio/blob/main/rasterio/session.py)); [TiTiler](https://github.com/developmentseed/titiler) — Set GDAL's AWS_S3_ENDPOINT, AWS_REGION and a read-only key in the TiTiler container environment; TiTiler reads COGs through GDAL /vsis3/ ([setup guide](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/titiler-cog-map-tiles)); [QGIS](https://qgis.org) — Add a raster layer with protocol type AWS S3 and set AWS_S3_ENDPOINT in its credential options, or set the GDAL AWS variables globally under Settings > Options > Variables ([setup guide](https://docs.qgis.org/latest/en/docs/user_manual/managing_data_source/opening_data.html)); [Esri ArcGIS Pro (cloud storage connection file)](https://doc.esri.com/en/arcgis-pro/latest/tool-reference/data-management/create-cloud-storage-connection-file.html) — Run Create Cloud Storage Connection File with service provider Amazon, the bucket name, a read-only key and Service End Point `s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`; Esri documents the custom endpoint for S3-compatible storage; [GeoServer COG community module](https://docs-archive.geoserver.org/stable/en/user/community/cog/cog.html) — Set IIO_<SCHEME>_AWS_ENDPOINT to `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`, where <SCHEME> matches the layer URL (S3 for s3://, HTTPS for https://), plus _AWS_USER, _AWS_PASSWORD and _AWS_REGION; install the COG community module; [Cloudflare CDN and Workers](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-cloudflare-integrations) — Point Cloudflare at the B2 bucket as origin; for private buckets, deploy a Worker that signs S3 requests with a scoped read-only key and passes range requests through ([setup guide](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/cloudflare-b2)).

**Scale:** Few large COGs per mission with many small concurrent range reads from viewers and tile servers. Standard B2 behind a CDN or tile cache is the default; tile caches absorb repeated reads. Measure sustained origin read rates before considering Overdrive.

**Security:** Tile servers accept validated layer ids, never arbitrary URLs, to avoid server-side request forgery; Each consumer gets a read-only key scoped to cog/ or a narrower prefix; Treat presigned COG URLs as bearer credentials with short TTLs; Private buckets behind a CDN use a signing Worker; do not make the bucket public to enable caching.

## Convert point clouds and meshes into streamable 3D datasets for web viewers

PDAL and Entwine clean, classify and convert photogrammetric and drone-LiDAR point clouds to COPC or EPT on B2 through s3:// paths, meshes and Gaussian splats for site digital twins are versioned alongside, and browser viewers stream them by range request from a public bucket or CDN.

**Use when:** Site and corridor point clouds are too large for clients to download. Teams need range-readable versions next to the source data for digital twins, volume measurement and construction progress.

**Workflow:** Source LAS/LAZ from NodeODM or a LiDAR payload lands in `pointcloud/<mission-id>/<run-id>/raw/` → A PDAL pipeline filters, classifies and reprojects, reading s3:// input and writing .copc.laz back through Arbiter with `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL=s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com` (host only; Arbiter prepends https://) → For multi-flight or very large sites, Entwine builds an EPT index into `pointcloud/<site>/ept/` through the same Arbiter S3 driver → Digital-twin jobs version camera poses, meshes and .ply splats under `twins/<site>/<capture-id>/` → Viewers (Potree, CesiumJS, COPC viewers) fetch by HTTP URL from a public bucket with CORS or through a CDN or signing Worker → Optionally, the twin is compared against IFC/BIM models to track construction progress

**B2 capabilities:** S3-compatible API with HTTP range GETs, CORS rules for browser viewers, Public bucket or CDN origin for multi-file tilesets, Multipart upload for multi-GB COPC/LAZ, Per-run versioned prefixes with manifests (B2-side pattern).

**Integrations:** [PDAL](https://pdal.io) — Set AWS_ENDPOINT_URL=`s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com` (host only; Arbiter prepends https://) or an endpoint key in Arbiter's JSON config; PDAL then reads and writes s3:// paths ([setup guide](https://github.com/PDAL/PDAL/blob/master/vendor/arbiter/arbiter.cpp)); [Entwine](https://github.com/connormanning/entwine) — Set AWS_ENDPOINT_URL=`s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com` (host only, no scheme); Entwine reads and writes s3:// paths through Arbiter ([setup guide](https://github.com/connormanning/arbiter/blob/master/arbiter/drivers/s3.cpp)); [Cloudflare CDN and Workers](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-cloudflare-integrations) — Point Cloudflare at the B2 bucket as origin; for private buckets, deploy a Worker that signs S3 requests with a scoped read-only key and passes range requests through ([setup guide](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/cloudflare-b2)).

**Scale:** Hundreds of MB to hundreds of GB per site, read by many small range requests from viewers. Standard B2 behind a CDN is the default. Per-file presigned URLs are impractical for multi-file octrees; prefer a CDN or signing Worker.

**Security:** Publish only cleared datasets to a public bucket; keep source clouds and twins private; Use a signing Worker with a read-only key for private tilesets; Processing keys cannot write outside pointcloud/ and twins/.

## Detect and geolocate defects in inspection imagery and video

YOLO or Roboflow Inference models scan inspection video and stills of towers, lines, solar farms, blades, bridges and roofs; geotagged detections, annotated keyframes, GeoJSON and Parquet roll-ups land in `inspections/<asset-id>/<inspection-id>/<model-version>/` and DuckDB queries them in place.

**Use when:** Each inspection video fans out into hundreds of derived objects across thousands of assets per season. Operators need results tied to source media and location, queryable fleet-wide, and reprocessable in batch when models improve.

**Workflow:** Source video and SRT/GPX telemetry land in raw/ (see flight-capture-offload) and the manifest event enqueues an inference job → The worker streams video from B2, samples keyframes, runs Ultralytics YOLO on a local GPU and extracts the GPS track from sidecar telemetry → It writes annotated keyframes, per-frame detection JSON, summary.json and a GeoJSON track to `inspections/<asset-id>/<inspection-id>/<model-version>/`; the review UI reads them by presigned GET → Edge variant - Roboflow Inference on a ground station or dock computer archives only flagged frames and prediction JSON, with hourly Parquet roll-ups under summaries/ → DuckDB httpfs with an S3 secret whose ENDPOINT is the B2 endpoint queries detection Parquet fleet-wide and writes slices back to `query-slices/` with COPY → When a better model ships, a batch job reprocesses the archive under a new model-version prefix

**B2 capabilities:** S3-compatible API with a regional endpoint, Multipart streaming upload for large video, Presigned GET for review UIs, Event Notifications to trigger inference, HTTP range reads for Parquet query in place, Object Lock for evidentiary inspection records, Write-only keys per edge device scoped to its prefix (`edge/<device>/`, `summaries/<device>/`).

**Integrations:** [AWS SDK for Python (boto3)](https://boto3.amazonaws.com/v1/documentation/api/latest/reference/core/session.html) — Set endpoint_url to `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com` derived from B2_REGION, and set request_checksum_calculation and response_checksum_validation to `when_required` in botocore Config; worker code uses boto3 to read frames and write inference results for Ultralytics and Roboflow ([setup guide](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-use-the-aws-sdk-for-python-with-backblaze-b2)); [DuckDB httpfs](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/core_extensions/httpfs/s3api.html) — CREATE SECRET of TYPE s3 with ENDPOINT `s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`, REGION and a scoped key; DuckDB reads Parquet row groups by range and writes results back with COPY.

**Scale:** Hundreds of derived objects per inspection across thousands of assets per season. Standard B2 is the default. Parquet roll-ups keep fleet-wide queries to a few range reads instead of listing millions of JSON objects.

**Security:** Edge devices hold write-only keys scoped to their own prefix, or receive presigned PUTs; Review UIs get short-lived presigned GETs; analysts get read-only keys; Reprocessing writes to a new model-version prefix and never overwrites earlier results.

## Label inspection frames and publish versioned defect-detection datasets

Flagged frames and orthomosaic chips are deduplicated, pre-labeled with SAM 2 or labeled in CVAT or Label Studio directly against B2, and exported as immutable dataset versions under `datasets/<name>/<version>/` next to versioned model checkpoints.

**Use when:** Defect classes such as cracks, corrosion, vegetation encroachment and thermal hot spots are rare and site-specific, so teams continuously relabel and retrain. They need labeling tools that read media from the archive without copying it and reproducible dataset versions tied to model versions.

**Workflow:** A curation job selects candidate frames from inspections/ and chips orthomosaic tiles; fastdup flags duplicates and outliers and quarantines them without deleting → SAM 2 writes pre-labeled masks into a draft label prefix → CVAT attaches B2 as Amazon S3 cloud storage with the B2 Endpoint URL, or Label Studio syncs source storage and writes annotations to target storage through its S3 Endpoint field → Reviewed labels are exported as COCO/YOLO to `datasets/<name>/<version>/` with a manifest of source keys and hashes; versions are never overwritten → Training workers cache shards on local NVMe, write checkpoints to `models/<name>/<version>/` and record the dataset version used → New model versions feed batch reprocessing in ai-inspection-detection

**B2 capabilities:** S3-compatible API with a regional endpoint, Presigned GET URLs for labeling UIs, CORS rules for browser annotation tools, Immutable versioned dataset prefixes with manifests (B2-side pattern), Object Lock (optional) on released dataset versions, Scoped keys per labeling tool (read media, write labels).

**Integrations:** [CVAT](https://docs.cvat.ai/docs/workspace/attach-cloud-storage/) — Attach cloud storage with provider Amazon S3, key ID and secret access key pair, and Endpoint URL `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`, as in CVAT's Backblaze B2 guide ([setup guide](https://docs.cvat.ai/docs/workspace/attach-cloud-storage/#attach-backblaze-b2-storage)); [Label Studio](https://labelstud.io/guide/storage_s3) — Set the S3 Endpoint field on source and target storage to `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`; serve media by presigned URLs (configure bucket CORS) or proxy it through Label Studio.

**Scale:** Thousands to millions of frames and chips per dataset version, read repeatedly during training. Standard B2 is the default; cache shards on local NVMe for multi-epoch training. Consider Overdrive only for sustained multi-GPU reads where storage throughput is the measured bottleneck.

**Security:** Labeling tools read media with list/read keys and write only to label prefixes; Do not grant deleteFiles to labeling tools; quarantine instead of deleting; Treat presigned media URLs as bearer credentials and restrict CORS to the tool's exact origin.

## Related sample applications

Sample applications for these storage workflows. Each linked repository includes source code and setup instructions.

- [OpenDroneMap Photogrammetry Pipeline](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/opendronemap-photogrammetry-pipeline): Presigned-PUT drone photo upload, local NodeODM reconstruction, and managed multipart write-back of orthomosaic, DEM, point cloud and mesh.
- [YOLO Drone Footage Detection](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/yolo-drone-footage-detection): Multipart video ingest, Ultralytics YOLO keyframe detection, GPX/SRT geotagging and a GeoJSON track on B2.
- [TiTiler COG Map Tiles](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/titiler-cog-map-tiles): GeoTIFF-to-COG conversion and dynamic XYZ tiles through GDAL /vsis3/ range reads with no stored tile copy.
- [Roboflow Inference Frame Archive](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/roboflow-inference-frame-archive): Edge inference that archives only flagged frames and prediction JSON, with hourly Parquet roll-ups.
- [YOLO11 Batch Detection Pipeline](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/yolo11-batch-detection-pipeline): Batch detection and segmentation over a B2 image and video library, writing COCO JSON, annotated frames and crops.
- [Open3D Point Cloud Pipeline](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/open3d-point-cloud-pipeline): PLY/PCD/LAS/LAZ ingest, downsampling, registration and meshing with a job manifest on B2.
- [COLMAP Photogrammetry Archive](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/colmap-photogrammetry-archive): pycolmap SfM that archives photos, database, sparse model and point cloud per project, served by presigned URL.
- [COLMAP Gaussian Splatting Pipeline](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/colmap-gaussian-splatting-pipeline): Photos or video to a COLMAP reconstruction and a Nerfstudio/gsplat-ready bundle versioned on B2.
- [SAM 2 Mask Dataset Builder](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/sam2-mask-dataset-builder): Versioned segmentation datasets built from a raw B2 media archive with local SAM 2.
- [fastdup Dataset Cleaning](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/fastdup-dataset-cleaning): Duplicate, outlier and corrupt-file detection with quality reports and quarantine without deleting originals.
- [DuckDB Query In Place](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/duckdb-query-in-place): SQL over Parquet, CSV and JSON in B2 through DuckDB httpfs, materializing results back as Parquet.
- [B2 Event Broker](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/b2-event-broker): Cloudflare Worker that validates signed B2 Event Notifications and fans them out to subscribers.
- [cloudflare-b2 (private bucket via Worker)](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/cloudflare-b2): Cloudflare Worker that signs range requests to a private B2 bucket for CDN delivery.
- [B2 Browser Upload](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/b2-browser-upload): Browser-direct upload by S3 presigned PUT or b2_upload_file through a Node.js back end (5 GB single-upload cap).
- [IfcOpenShell BIM Archive](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/ifcopenshell-bim-archive): IFC models, meshes and reports per project with manifests, served by presigned URL.
